items.title: Here's what happened in crypto today
items.summary: Daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Trump taps intel chief Jay Clayton to lead new Super Intelligence Force
items.summary: President Donald Trump said US intel chief Clayton will lead the SIF, reporting to the president and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

items.title: Japan adds Garantex to list of Russia sanctions over Ukraine war
items.summary: Garantex was previously sanctioned by the US, the EU and other jurisdictions for helping Russian entities evade financial restrictions.

items.title: El Salvador receives USD 138 million from IMF after Bitcoin waivers granted
items.summary: Efforts will continue to reduce the state's involvement in Bitcoin-related activities and to strengthen cryptoasset regulation and governance, the IMF said.

items.title: Russia's Finance Ministry pays wages in digital rubles for first time
items.summary: Work on the introduction of the digital ruble to the budget process is being carried out by the Bank of Russia together with the Ministry of Finance.

items.title: NEAR Intents recovers entire stolen USD 3.8M after ultimatum to exploiter
items.summary: The exploiter returned the entire sum to NEAR Intents after being identified and given 48 hours to respond.

items.title: Trump Taps Jay Clayton, the SEC Chair Who Sued Ripple, to Lead AI Push
items.summary: President Trump named a Super Intelligence Force to coordinate federal AI policy, with Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton at the helm.

items.title: Banking Group Sues to Block Crypto's 'Side Door' Into the Banking System
items.summary: The Independent Community Bankers of America argues the OCC's national trust charters give crypto firms a side door into the banking system.

items.title: 'Uptober' Starts Green as Bitcoin ETFs Draw USD 134 Million
items.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs took in USD 134.4 million over the first two trading days of October, rebounding from a Sept. 30 outflow as a weak jobs report cooled Fed rate-hike bets.

items.title: 'We Have Identified You, Sir': Near Intents Recovers USD 3.8 Million After 48-Hour Ultimatum
items.summary: Near Intents said the roughly USD 3.8 million drained in an exploit on Thursday was returned in full after a 48-hour ultimatum.

items.title: Chainalysis Used AI to Trace the USD 387M Bitget Hack Back to North Korea
items.summary: The firm says the Sept. 24 breach pushed North Korea's 2026 crypto haul past USD 1 billion. Title cites USD 387M; URL slug cites 87m. Not a desk number.

items.title: OpenAI Banned PewDiePie Twice While He Built Ajax, an Uncensored AI That Will Run on Your PC
items.summary: The YouTuber says OpenAI suspended his account twice while he trained a small, uncensored model built to run on your own computer.

items.title: Drift opens exploit recovery claims with initial payouts of just over 1% of user losses
items.summary: DFX holders can cash out now or wait for more funding, with no firm timeline for full repayment.

items.title: Paradigm-backed Layer 2 Blast to wind down network as costs exceed revenue
items.summary: Ethereum L2 Blast is winding down after costs outpaced revenue. Users have until Oct. 26 to withdraw via the app.

items.title: Bitcoin nears highest level since January as USD 85,000 sell wall clears, US jobs data disappoints
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed back toward USD 87,000 on Friday as sellers cleared out around USD 85,000, according to Glassnode. Not a desk price.

items.title: BitGo CEO says Clarity's failure left capital markets exposed to risk potentially worse than Lehman
items.summary: BitGo CEO Mike Belshe warned that Clarity's failure left systemic risks arising from one firm holding exchange, brokerage, and custody functions.

items.title: ECB outlines three models for putting central bank money onchain
items.summary: The ECB outlined three models for bringing central bank money onchain as financial institutions explore settlement infrastructure.

items.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs log USD 2.7 billion in September inflows as institutional demand holds
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded USD 2.65 billion in net inflows in September, their second-largest monthly inflow since October 2025.

items.title: Bitcoin's USD 85,000 recovery awaits proof that ETF investors kept buying after payrolls
items.summary: Glassnode estimated the probability of an additional quarter-point hike at the Oct. 28 meeting fell from 66 percent on Sept. 28 to 22 percent by 15:00 UTC on Oct. 2. Not a desk price.

items.title: Bitcoin Core's new fix closes gap that could redirect funds without stealing keys
items.summary: A missing-output SIGHASH_SINGLE request can leave recipients unbound; Core's merged PSBT repair has no confirmed fixed-release destination.

items.title: New Treasury rules could change how stablecoin issuers get your dollars back
items.summary: Washington is rewriting rules for borrowing against government debt, and the result will reach crypto through stablecoin issuers.

items.title: India's local crypto exchanges get just 0.7% of inflows, Chainalysis reports
items.summary: Chainalysis regional chapters separate national crypto participation from domestic exchange business. Brazil platforms cited at 12.5 percent of inflows.

items.title: Drift hack recovery opened near one cent per dollar lost
items.summary: Drift's October 1 launch quote valued DFX near one cent per USDT lost, while redemption ends future pool participation for the tokens burned.

items.title: Vitalik-inspired AI payment system can send expired deposits to its treasury
items.summary: zkAPI offers an exit without server clearance, but challenged spending states, vault pauses and note expiry can constrain recovery.

items.title: IMF Praises El Salvador - But Still Tries To Scale Back Its Bitcoin Project
items.summary: The IMF approved a USD 139 million disbursement to El Salvador but still wants it to scale back its Bitcoin project.

items.title: When the Banks Don't Work, Bitcoin Does: Cornell University's Adoption Index
items.summary: Cornell University spoke to 25,880 people about using bitcoin. Many do not understand the tech in depth; some find it useful.

items.title: South Africa's Absa Becomes First Bank on the Continent to Custody Bitcoin: Report
items.summary: South African bank Absa has become the first African lender to custody bitcoin, according to reports.

items.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Above USD 87,000 on Softer-Than-Expected Jobs Data
items.summary: Headline print: bitcoin surged above USD 87,000 on Friday in New York on ETF flows and a softer jobs report. Not a desk price.

items.title: Impacts of Daily Dividends on Digital Credit
items.summary: Analyzing the implications for digital credit instruments paying daily dividends.

items.title: Frank Holmes: They Will Print USD 100 Trillion - Why to Buy Bitcoin & Gold
items.summary: HIVE's Frank Holmes on mining sites, former Ethereum GPUs, and the AI boom. Headline only. DO NOT BUY from a headline.

items.title: There's an election next month: State of Crypto
items.summary: Congress is gone from Washington for the final pre-election recess, and it's time to take stock of what's going on ahead of November.

items.title: Crypto poured years into new products. The next challenge is keeping users
items.summary: Crypto firms have spent years building financial products on blockchains. Getting people to use them is the next challenge.

items.title: The Clarity Act stalled. Bankers aren't hitting the brakes yet on crypto dealmaking
items.summary: Crypto M&A has hit record levels, but the Clarity Act's Senate setback leaves dealmakers weighing regulatory uncertainty.

items.title: Payments firm OpenPayd targets year-end Nasdaq listing to fund U.S. expansion and acquisitions
items.summary: CEO Iana Dimitrova said OpenPayd aims to launch in the U.S. by April 2027 and is eyeing deals to add licenses and technology.

items.title: Crypto job postings triple to over 1,200 in September, but applications fall
items.summary: Finance, engineering and trading led hiring demand. Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana were the most frequently requested blockchain skills.

items.title: Cathie Wood says smart investors need to start watching where AI agents spend money
items.summary: As AI agents evolve from answering questions to spending real money, investors are watching the networks behind machine-driven commerce.
